solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Firm friend admits writing articles in attempt to limit damage

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: a friend who admits something lets it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a mate is a friend
pens are articles used for writing

explanation.surface: A company and an ally try to contain the harm done by some published pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' is the containment signal. 'Writing articles' looks like journalism but means implements for writing; 'in attempt to' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends or offset a loss is to cap the harm done, the usual sense of making good.

clue.text: Area in a Green uprising where low-lying islands abound

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the string from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
eco- is a prefix meaning environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: An environmental party gains ground in a region of atolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns the string A + IN + A + ECO upwards; 'Green' looks like a political party but supplies ECO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific region including Polynesia, Micronesia and Melanesia is famous for its coral atolls barely above sea level.

clue.text: Silver penny no longer in circulation?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
the late are dead, no longer going about among us

explanation.surface: An old silver coin that has been withdrawn from use.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a withdrawn coin, but 'no longer in circulation' describes someone deceased: LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Household tableware made of or coated in precious metal is collectively called by this word.

clue.text: Something obnoxious exists to split subtle difference

indicators.note: the short word splits the longer one by sitting between its letters

parts.note: a nuance is a fine shade of difference
is means exists

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant is drawing a hair-splitting distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to split' is the containment signal: the short verb sits inside the fine distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest or annoyance is something objectionable that bothers people.

clue.text: Mammal teasing in incredibly powerful attraction

indicators.note: behaving incredibly, beyond belief, these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A furry creature being teased in a remarkably appealing way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incredibly' looks like an intensifier for 'powerful' but signals the anagram of MAMMAL TEASING IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means charisma or strong physical allure, from Mesmer's theory of a magnetic life force.

clue.text: Buñuel's The Constant Cardinal

parts.note: Luis Buñuel was a Spanish film director, and the Spanish for 'the' is el (also the title of one of his films)
even means constant or steady

explanation.surface: Reads like the title of a Buñuel film about a steadfast churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman but means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are counting numbers, and this is one of them, the one after ten.

clue.text: Wild cat's course by the sea given mention

indicators.note: something given a mention is spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: links is a golf course on sandy coastal land

explanation.surface: A golf course by the coast is named after a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A links is a seaside golf course, as at St Andrews in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-tailed wild feline with tufted ears found in northern forests.

clue.text: Cut a liver out — it's producing profit

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Organ removal for money: a grisly trade in livers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'cut out' but signals the anagram of CUT A LIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that brings in money or yields gain is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Bread head gets past capital

parts.note: naan or nan is South Asian flatbread
a king is a head of state

explanation.surface: A baker's chief moves beyond the main city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' just links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese city served as the national seat of government in earlier periods, so it is a former capital.

clue.text: Sixth letter to Greeks, seventh to follow our last

indicators.note: the seventh Greek letter is placed to follow, after, the Z

parts.note: Z is the last letter of our alphabet
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A lesson in alphabet order, Greek against English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seventh' carries over from 'to Greeks': the seventh Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek alphabet, the letter after epsilon stands in sixth place.

clue.text: One looking into Irish ancestry gets shot

indicators.note: one thing looking into another is placed within it

parts.note: descent means lineage or ancestry
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A genealogist researching Irish roots is gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking into' is the containment signal. 'shot' means shimmering, as in shot silk, whose colour changes with the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot fabric shows shifting colours depending on the angle, which is exactly what this rainbow-like adjective describes.

clue.text: Say Merkel makes investor apprehensive at first

parts.note: an angel is a backer who invests in a show or start-up

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: The German chancellor makes a financier nervous at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Merkel as an example of people with this first name: Angela Merkel, former German chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, of which the former German chancellor is a famous example.

clue.text: On tree-lined road Frau von Trapp offers prayer

parts.note: AVE is short for avenue, a road traditionally lined with trees
Maria von Trapp is the heroine of The Sound of Music

explanation.surface: Maria von Trapp prays on a leafy avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' and 'offers' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is a Catholic devotion addressed to the Virgin, known by its Latin opening words.

clue.text: This can be hot music, rocking on beat

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: to cap is to beat or outdo

indicators.note: music that is rocking is being shaken about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hot rock music with a strong beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' is the anagram signal, and 'on' places the result after the word for beat. 'hot' sounds like a description of music but means spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppers of this genus range from sweet to fiery, so some are spicy.

clue.text: Appropriate search within bishopric on river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the river letter
the search is placed within the bishopric

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: A suitable search is carried out within a diocese beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' is the containment signal. 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to take possession of.
explanation.definitionFit: To confiscate or seize assets is a legal sense of taking them into custody.

clue.text: Scandinavian girl in Guam oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, the first and third

explanation.surface: A Nordic woman somewhere in the Pacific island of Guam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes G and A from GUAM.
explanation.definitionFit: This female forename is common in Sweden, Norway and Denmark.

clue.text: Party favourite comes to power

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a minion was originally a favourite of a monarch

explanation.surface: A party's favoured candidate gains office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minion' is used in its old sense of a royal favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovereignty or rule over a territory is authority, control.

clue.text: Republican organisation put before Queen and Country

indicators.note: the organisation is placed before the queen's letter

parts.note: the IRA, Irish Republican Army, is an Irish republican organisation
Q is an abbreviation for queen, as in chess

explanation.surface: A republican group prioritising itself over Queen and Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen and Country' is a stock patriotic phrase; here they split into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation with Baghdad as its capital is a country.

clue.text: What suggests our US is causing destruction?

parts.note: putting the letters R and U inside O-U-S, after OU, spells these two clue words run together

explanation.surface: Asks what implies ownership of America is wrecking things.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer as RU IN OUS and follow it as an instruction, and it produces 'our US'; 'What suggests' points at that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disastrous or devastating brings about wreckage or ruin.

clue.text: In GB, show great affection for cattle in lab's toxic container

indicators.note: the affection word is placed in the letters GB

parts.note: to love is to show great affection for
an ox is one of the cattle

explanation.surface: A British farmer adores livestock kept in a laboratory's sealed cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts LOVE between G and B. A lab glove box is a sealed case with built-in gloves for handling hazardous material.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed chamber with fixed gauntlets lets scientists handle hazardous substances safely.

clue.text: Shocking fuss after outside broadcast

indicators.note: the fuss comes after the broadcast

parts.note: making a scene is causing a fuss

explanation.surface: An appalling row follows a live television report from on location.
explanation.walkthrough: An outside broadcast is a TV or radio programme made on location.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd or offensive material is described as outrageous and shocking.

clue.text: Trouble had upset lovely thing in bed

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters over, reading upward

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A troubled night upset a pleasant time in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns both words upward. 'bed' sounds like sleeping but is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy garden flower grown in borders and flower beds, prized for its blooms.

clue.text: Barker's first-rate ginger beer

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
ginger hair is red
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A top-quality ginger beer from someone called Barker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger beer' looks like one drink but splits into a colour and a drink; A1 gives AI with the digit read as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large terrier breed from Yorkshire, and dogs bark.

clue.text: I seek avian habitat lined with good down

indicators.note: a nest lined with something has it inside

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone looking for a bird's nest lined with soft feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lined with' puts G inside NEST. 'down' looks like soft feathers but is the verb, to swallow; 'seek' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To down food or drink is to swallow it, taking it into the body.

clue.text: Infantryman emptied latrine over southern chap

indicators.note: in a down clue the emptied latrine sits over the S

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside, leaving only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A foot soldier on latrine duty in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves the L and E of LATRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, and a chap is any man.

clue.text: Back home, unwell after rich cake and pasta

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the cake

parts.note: a torte is a rich layered cake

indicators.note: back means the following words are read backwards

parts.note: in means at home
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Back home and ill after overindulging in cake and pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the home and unwell words round to make LLINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Small ring-shaped stuffed pasta shapes from Italy.

clue.text: Edible plant's supplied by member in ship coming about

indicators.note: a ship coming about turns round, so the word is turned around

parts.note: the keel is the main structural member running along the bottom of a ship

explanation.surface: A vegetable supplied by a crew member aboard a ship that is changing course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a crew member but is a structural member: the keel. 'coming about' is a sailing term for turning.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion-family vegetable with a long white stem, eaten cooked.

clue.text: Addict taken in because relapsed

indicators.note: the letters are taken in, contained, within the clue words

explanation.surface: An addict admitted to treatment after a relapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like rehab admission but signals letters within BECAUSE RELAPSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes drugs habitually is called by this word in slang.

clue.text: Notice upright character in cathedral gets control

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: the upright letter goes in the cathedral word

parts.note: a minster is a large church or cathedral, as at York
I is the letter that stands upright like a single stroke

explanation.surface: A notice in a cathedral says someone upright takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; the upright character is I, which looks like a single standing stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or run affairs, to be in charge of them, is to direct them.
